entities.summary: Llywelyn ap Merfyn was a pivotal figure in early 10th-century Welsh history, serving as the King of Powys from 950 to 942 CE. His reign was marked by significant power struggles with neighboring kingdoms and a struggle for control over the strategic location of the kingdom of Deheubarth. Llywelyn ap Merfyn's reign was also notable for the efforts to strengthen the Welsh church and promote the spread of Christianity in Wales. His legacy has had a lasting impact on the development of the Welsh language and culture, with many Welsh dynasties claiming descent from him. The 10th-century Welsh chronicles, such as the Annales Cambriae, provide valuable insights into Llywelyn ap Merfyn's life and reign, offering a glimpse into the complex web of alliances, conflicts, and cultural exchange that defined the medieval Welsh world.
